title: Version control and reproducible C builds
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its constraints.
Trace the example and reason about its data flow.
Identify complexity, boundary or safety considerations.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Version control records source changes and supports review, rollback and collaboration. A reproducible build documents compiler version, flags, dependencies and source inputs so another environment can rebuild the program consistently.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable C engineering requires knowing exactly which source and toolchain produced a binary. Version history also makes risky changes easier to inspect and revert.
understand.analogy: Treat an algorithm or data structure as a set of operations that must preserve a clearly stated contract.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace formal complexity analysis, C object rules or algorithm preconditions.

explain.narrative:
Version control records source changes and supports review, rollback and collaboration. A reproducible build documents compiler version, flags, dependencies and source inputs so another environment can rebuild the program consistently.

Before implementation, state input constraints, empty-case behaviour, ownership and invariants. Compile with warnings and test representative, boundary and failure cases.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The Makefile records a compiler variable, flags and source dependencies. A real project should also document generated files and external library requirements.

practise.guidedTask: Identify the inputs that affect the build output.
practise.independentTask: Create a small repository with a Makefile, README build instructions and a test command.
hints: Commit source and build configuration, not generated secrets or machine-specific temporary files.
Record compiler and dependency versions when reproducibility matters.
Review diffs before committing and test the committed revision.
